challenges.title: The emergency exception and the 144-hour cap

items.title: The emergency exception to the 2-hour daily limit
items.text: The regular daily limit of 2 hours' overtime may be exceeded where the work is necessary to prevent a serious loss or accident, or to mitigate its consequences (Art. 19) — the 144-hour cap per 3-week period still remains the hard ceiling.

items.title: Gap-free ward coverage around the clock
items.text: Day, evening and night shifts must be staffed without gaps across every ward — made harder still by short-notice emergency call-outs.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off hospitals in the UAE
solutions.subtitle: From a properly documented emergency exception to gap-free ward coverage — everything works together.

items.title: Gap-free 24/7 ward coverage
items.text: Day, evening and night shifts across every ward — Klacks flags every gap immediately and can fill it automatically on request.

items.title: Emergency overtime recorded separately
items.text: Emergency call-outs that exceed the regular 2-hour daily limit can be recorded separately in Klacks with notes on the reason — traceable, not blanket.

items.title: The 144-hour total continuously visible
items.text: Klacks continuously totals working hours per 3-week period and makes them visible — even where emergency call-outs are involved, so you can keep the 144-hour cap in view yourself.

items.title: Qualifications factored in automatically
items.text: Every shift is only assigned to staff with the matching qualification — with no manual checking at all.

items.title: On-premise: data stays in-house
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure. Staff and patient data never leave the hospital — not even for the AI.

items.title: Klacksy schedules by voice
items.text: "Fill next week's night shifts for the ward" is all it takes — Klacksy automatically factors in qualifications and shows the 144-hour total.

example.title: The emergency exception and the 144-hour cap, at a glance
example.text: An emergency call-out that exceeds the 2-hour daily limit can be recorded separately in Klacks together with the reason, while total working hours per 3-week period remain continuously visible — no manual recalculating required.
